requirements.text: Conformance MUST identify the implemented profile, its version, the reader, and the assessed scope.
A serializer MAY organize them differently if its mapping preserves their obligations.
An empty list MUST mean an established empty set within a declared scope.
It MUST NOT stand for an unknown set.
A profile MAY represent a genuinely irrelevant group as not applicable with a reason.
It MUST NOT silently omit a required obligation because no evidence is available.
Each constraint MUST have an identity, subject, scope, predicate or human-readable rule, source of authority when relevant, severity, and a checking method or an explicit unresolved status.
An implementation MUST retain its applicability conditions and dependencies.
A constraint can also be an acceptance obligation, but the relationship MUST be explicit.

When profiles compose, all applicable mandatory constraints MUST remain in force unless an identified authority, authenticated at the same declared trust boundary as evidence, has explicitly resolved a conflict within its verified authority.
Load order, a later paragraph, or a more convenient result MUST NOT implicitly override a restriction.
A reader MUST advertise supported representations and required extensions.
A reader MUST derive requiredness from the trusted request/policy and known constraint references as well as profile declarations, and MUST block an unknown constraint-bearing profile.
Only an extension established as irrelevant to every mandatory obligation MAY be retained as optional opaque data, with the limitation reported.
Admission MUST evaluate the exact contract revision, requirements, recipient, environment, applicable constraints, mandatory dependencies, and current authority.
Unknown MUST NOT be promoted to pass.
A conforming execution adapter MUST validate evidence provenance at its declared trust boundary.
Unmapped fields and semantic losses MUST be reported.
Refusal reports SHOULD identify the failed obligation and an actionable reason without exposing protected grounds to an unauthorized recipient.
An implementation MUST NOT create a success-shaped output when assembly, authorization, or evidence checking fails.

A conformance suite MUST include: a supported positive request; a missing required dependency; an unknown required profile; a conflicting constraint; an outdated requirement revision; an unauthorized executor; mismatched output evidence; a migration with unknown values; and a false claim of trusted evidence.
Schema, internal consistency, applicability, and execution acceptance MUST be reported separately.
This document specifies operation semantics; a conforming adapter MUST also identify its representation profile and executable checks.
Every operation definition MUST identify the following:
Preconditions, invariants and postconditions MUST remain separate.
An implementation MAY expose narrower operations within these families.
Every exposed operation MUST state which of these responsibilities it owns and which it delegates.
It MUST NOT hide a necessary responsibility between adapters.
For operations A then B, every allowed successful output of A used by B MUST satisfy B's preconditions.
A shared invariant MUST survive both transitions.
A semantic transformation MUST declare its protected observations: for example the truth conditions of a proposition, the order of procedural steps, or the labels and connections of a diagram.
Lossy transformations MUST retain a loss account.
A timeout after dispatch MUST preserve an unknown-effect state until a domain-specific reconciliation establishes what occurred.
These dimensions MUST NOT be collapsed into a single completion flag.
Evidence MUST identify the definition version, input and output revisions, attempt, relevant requirements, checker and check result.
An inherited observation MUST name the premise that permits inheritance.
Checks of supplied claims and checks of independently observed conditions MUST be distinguishable.

A conforming adapter MUST exercise valid input; invalid input; unknown mandatory preconditions; a protected-property violation; partial output; an exhausted budget; a stale requirement revision; and, for effectful operations, a timeout with uncertain effect.
A composition test MUST include a valid A output that violates B's precondition.
Legacy example envelopes remain interpretable under their original profiles; an adapter MUST disclose any loss when mapping them to this family.
This specification defines the distinctions an implementation MUST preserve when interpreting and representing knowledge.
A conforming profile MUST state its vocabulary, cardinalities and representation mapping.
A profile MAY store several dimensions in one structured record, but MUST NOT conflate their meanings.
For each required facet, the profile MUST distinguish known value, unknown value, justified not applicable, and withheld value.
Withheld indicates a disclosure boundary and MUST NOT be represented as evidence that no value exists.
Extraction boundaries MUST follow the obligations of the intended interpretation.
Source identity, semantic object identity, representation identity and retrieval chunk identity MUST remain distinguishable.
Relations MUST identify their endpoints and kind.
A vague association MUST NOT be silently upgraded to a proof premise, causal link or authority relation.
Operators MUST bind to their actual scope.
When several interpretations remain possible, an implementation MUST retain the alternatives or mark the interpretation unresolved.
A media reference MUST identify the representation revision and selector semantics.
Required legends, ordering, coordinate conventions, units and joint components MUST be retained.
A profile MUST record which was inspected.

The conformance suite MUST include an attributed false assertion, a scoped negation, a quotation inside another quotation, a counterexample with tempting instructional wording, an unresolved alternative reading, and a required media dependency omitted from delivery.
Vocabulary mappings MUST state whether they are exact, broader, narrower or merely related.

A conforming package MUST contain or reference its identity and revision; task and requirements revision; purpose and recipient; source and corpus snapshots; selected unit revisions; mandatory dependency closure; slot-level coverage; declared search scope and assurance; applicable constraints; representation and delivery requirements; resource account; and the observations supporting its status.
Each requirement slot MUST identify the subject, quantifier, required conditions and supporting units.
Joint requirements MUST be supported for the same subject and revision.
The package MUST identify omitted requirements and unresolved dependencies.
The finite set-theoretic closure exists even with cycles, but a particular executable profile MAY require an acyclic dependency graph.
That restriction MUST be stated and checked.
A composer MUST recalculate closure and budget after a change.
It MUST NOT infer that a larger text is always safer or more useful: additional content may conflict, distract, disclose protected information or exceed the recipient's usable capacity.
Each report MUST bind to its own stage and subject revision.
An empty top-k result MUST NOT be reported as proof of global absence.

The budget MUST account for the actual delivery context: system and task instructions, relevant history, selected material, tool descriptions, anticipated tool results, output allowance and margin where applicable.
Estimated and measured quantities MUST be distinguishable and identify the tokenizer or measurement method.
A projection MUST retain protected units, their relations and task-relevant uncertainty.
It MUST identify excluded units and losses.
When the mandatory closure cannot fit, the composer MUST return a partial result, negotiate an allowed narrower scope, change representation with justified preservation, or refuse.
It MUST NOT silently discard a mandatory condition to meet the limit.
The delivery check MUST match the task's representation requirements and the declared reader capabilities.
Any output assessment MUST name the exact delivered package and requirements revision.

Acceptance cases MUST include an unresolved dependency, cross-object conjunction, missing quantifier coverage, a budget overflow caused by closure, omitted mandatory media, an outdated requirement revision, and a final output that drops a supported condition.
For each, the check MUST distinguish package construction from downstream use.

A conformance claim MUST identify the artifact kind, representation profile and checks performed. [Controlled knowledge reuse](../../../papers/controlled-knowledge-reuse/PAPER.md) provides the model; [cache identity](../cache-identity-and-invalidation/SPECIFICATION.md) and [reuse policy](../reuse-policy/SPECIFICATION.md) govern later applications.
An extension MUST state its additional obligations and compatibility rules.

The artifact MUST identify immutable output bytes or a precisely canonicalized structured value, its hash domain, representation profile, content identity, source and rule-set revisions, recipe identity, and the producing attempt.
The build recipe MUST include exact input references, transformation definition versions, relevant parameters, and environment dependencies that can change the claimed result.

An attempt record MUST distinguish the `planned`, `ready`, `running`, `paused` and `finished` execution phases from the [status model](../status-model/SPECIFICATION.md#3-canonical-dimension-vocabularies); outcome; stop reason; output references if any; and observed effects.
A failed attempt MUST NOT create a fictional successful artifact.
The manifest MUST include each declared dependency's identity, revision, role, requirement status, relevant validity conditions and change sensitivity.
A result based on absence or exhaustive enumeration MUST bind the universe or index snapshot and completeness procedure.
The manifest MUST distinguish a navigational citation from an operational dependency.
It SHOULD explain why each operational dependency is material, so a reviewer can identify both missing dependencies and unjustified over-invalidation.
Parameter substitution MUST NOT remove scope, change a protected quantifier or carry authority from one recipient to another without an explicit rule.
Evidence MUST bind to the exact artifact and check.

Publishing a mutable current pointer MUST follow the complete atomic predicate in [cache identity §5](../cache-identity-and-invalidation/SPECIFICATION.md#5-guarded-publication-and-serving), including dependency and authority epochs in the same decision as the head update.
A build that finished successfully under an old generation MUST NOT overwrite a newer or revoked head.
The final admission decision MUST be valid at the actual serve boundary, not only when the build began.

A conformance suite MUST cover an altered input with an unchanged lookup key, a recipe change, an unsuccessful build, a template parameter outside its domain, a stale publication generation, a negative result invalidated by corpus growth, and evidence for the wrong output.
The expected result MUST be an explicit new build, refusal, unresolved state or valid guarded reuse under a named policy.
A migration MUST retain the old artifact and hash domain, identify the mapping and its losses, and create a new representation record.
Every current artifact MUST live in a uniquely named directory within its type collection.
Directory names use meaningful lowercase words separated by single hyphens; a reader MUST be able to infer the topic without looking up an internal number.
Historical identifiers MAY remain in provenance and migration maps.
Current publications MUST appear in `publication-catalog.json`.
Each main Markdown file MUST have YAML front matter with `name`, `title`, `artifact`, `edition`, `author`, `language`, `license`, and a nonempty `description`.
It MUST contain one descriptive H1.
Version and machine identifiers belong in metadata, compatibility notes or provenance; they MUST NOT dominate the reading title.
Provider-specific executable agent configurations MUST have an explicit adapter and remain distinct from the human-readable role definition.
Each registered revision MUST identify its kind, representation profile, identity, revision, license or disclosure restriction, provenance, required dependencies and applicable observations.
A reader MUST distinguish known, unknown, not applicable and withheld information.
Required references MUST resolve to the intended revision or report an unresolved dependency.
Registry checks MUST reject duplicate canonical names, missing required main files, incompatible front matter, broken current links and silent identity reuse.
A rename test MUST show where the previous path leads and how a cited immutable revision remains recoverable.
Migration MUST preserve source identity and original revisions, record the mapping, and disclose fields that could not be translated.
It MUST NOT infer a capability, grant or successful execution from the presence of an artifact.
A profile MUST select the dimensions needed for its purpose and declare any aggregation rule.
Each observation MUST identify its subject and immutable revision, assessed property, requirements or criterion revision, method, observer, relevant time, result, grounds and limits.
If the method trusts supplied input rather than independently authenticating it, that assumption MUST be stated.
A positive result MUST NOT overwrite a negative or unresolved result on another mandatory property.
A profile using the current tokens MUST use the snake_case values below without overloading one dimension with another.
An older profile MAY retain its original lexical values only through an explicit, loss-reporting adapter.

Legacy labels MUST map explicitly: `terminated` → run phase `finished`; `unsupported in scope` → coverage `unsupported`; “incomplete execution of planned search” → `incomplete_procedure`; `not_measured` → assessment `unknown` with reason “no observation.” Profile-specific quality states such as book-package `reviewed` retain their own declared scope; they are not aliases for `pass`.
Implementations MUST follow the tables; transitions not listed are rejected.
Every transition MUST record the triggering observation, actor, prior state and guard result.
A finished attempt MUST NOT return to running; retry uses a new attempt with a repeat policy.
New projection records MAY replace the current display only while preserving the observations on which earlier displays were based.
An expired or ineligible observation MUST NOT be overwritten merely because another record has a later timestamp.
These transitions MUST NOT change truth, review, freshness or eligibility by themselves.
The vocabulary MUST NOT equate “published,” “reviewed,” “implemented,” and “effective.”
An internal agent review MUST identify the reviewer, input revision, method and conclusions, and MUST be labelled as such.
An executed failed trial remains useful evidence and MUST retain its negative result.
Interfaces MAY summarize these dimensions, but the summary MUST preserve the distinctions relevant to the user's decision.

“Indexed revision X” is more precise than an unqualified “current.” “Checks passed for the supplied record” MUST NOT become “the action is authorized” when current authorization was outside the checked boundary.
An unknown effect after a timeout MUST remain visible when a user decides whether to retry.

Tests MUST cover a passed schema with false supplied grounds, successful execution with a failed result criterion, a finished run with unknown effect, a resident but revoked artifact, a correct historical result ineligible for a current task, and an internal review that does not establish empirical validity.
An exchange record MUST be a single strict UTF-8 JSON object without a BOM, duplicate member names at any depth, non-finite number tokens or isolated Unicode surrogates.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Integers used as epochs or sequence numbers MUST be in 0 through 9,007,199,254,740,991.
Implementations MUST compare schema/profile support before exchanging records.
They MUST NOT infer support for an entire contract family from support for this subset.
Identity comparisons MUST include both domain and digest.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: This profile deliberately does not define value-level canonical JSON hashing; a profile that needs it MUST name a separate procedure and domain.
Every implementation MUST state its consistency assumptions and failure behavior.
A lookup MUST be followed by request/artifact descriptor comparison and the required admission checks.
A digest collision assumption and the selected byte or canonical-value domain MUST be stated when digest equality is used as identity evidence.
The descriptor comparison MUST return an itemized `pass`, `fail`, `unknown` or justified `not_applicable` for the relevant components.
The algorithm MUST NOT equate two requests merely because their lookup key, text embedding or source bytes agree.

The read set MUST contain every declared dependency material to the claimed reuse guarantee, including source revisions, required selectors, profiles, rules, request requirements, compiler behavior and authorization state.
Negative results and exhaustive claims MUST also track their universe or index generation and completeness assumptions.
Unknown impact MUST produce re-evaluation or a conservative unresolved result under the policy.
It MUST NOT be inferred harmless simply because the old key still matches.
Epochs are nonnegative integers and a relevant change MUST strictly advance the affected dependency epoch even when its content bytes are unchanged.
`new_epoch` MUST exceed `old_epoch`; `revoked` events MUST carry `impact: blocked`.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: A receiver MUST deduplicate an identical event identifier only when the complete event bytes agree, detect conflicting reuse of that identifier, and treat a missing or reordered sequence in its declared ordering namespace as a reconciliation requirement.
If event loss is possible, reconciliation MUST compare observed dependency state with authoritative state before renewing affected admission claims.
A disconnected system MAY serve under an explicitly bounded policy, but MUST NOT claim immediate global revocation when its consistency protocol cannot establish it.
Generation values MUST NOT be reused after rollback, restart, restore or counter exhaustion.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: A runtime unable to recover the counter safely MUST establish a fresh namespace and invalidate old read sets.
A worker's read set MUST contain the namespace and generation, every material dependency's exact revision and epoch, and relevant authority/policy epochs.

Publication MUST make one linearizable decision over the following predicate: the current namespace and head generation equal the worker's expected values; every declared material dependency still has the observed epoch/revision; current authority and policy permit this exact output/use; and all required build checks remain satisfied.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: The head update and increment of generation MUST occur atomically with that decision.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Every relevant revocation MUST advance its authority/dependency epoch and the affected head generation within the declared decision boundary.
A late worker MUST NOT restore an older head, undo a revocation or publish against an unchanged-looking dependency after an intervening change.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: A deployment lacking an atomic boundary over these conditions MUST fail closed or explicitly offer a weaker named consistency profile; it cannot claim this strict guarantee.
The serve guard MUST validate the exact output, relevant current dependency epochs and current authority at the actual serve consistency point.
A lease MUST define scope, expiry, revocation behavior, clock assumptions and partition behavior.
Recovery MUST verify content identity and rebuild the current eligibility decision rather than restoring a historical positive verdict as current fact.
Logs SHOULD record lookup candidate, compared descriptors, dependency observations, admission decision, publication generation and actual serve result.
Logging MUST respect the recipient's disclosure rights.
Each test MUST identify the simulated or real consistency boundary.
A reuse policy determines whether a saved result may satisfy a new request, what MUST be rechecked, and which time and authority constraints apply.

Before deciding freshness, the policy MUST establish semantic compatibility with the request, required dependency availability, applicable constraints, current disclosure authorization and any action-specific grant.
Service availability MUST NOT silently choose a weaker temporal mode.
The policy MUST distinguish source-event time, source-observation time, artifact-build time, check time, authorization interval and storage time.
Times MUST use one declared clock and unit.
Bounds and durations MUST be finite; intervals require lower ≤ upper, and TTL and permitted maximum age require nonnegative values.
A policy MUST identify each deadline's class and basis.
A failed refresh MUST NOT reset either deadline.

Invalid intervals (lower > upper), a definitely future check (`checked.lower > now.upper`), negative durations, incompatible clocks or unknown mandatory bounds MUST yield `unresolved` without an admitted serve.
Where order itself is mandatory, overlapping intervals that cannot establish `checked.upper <= now.lower` also remain unresolved; an implementation MUST NOT invent a chronology from point estimates.
A stale fallback MUST NOT conceal known semantic invalidity, a hard expiry or revocation.
A utility estimate MUST state its task, baseline, horizon, units and included costs.
Build, retrieval, validation, maintenance and integration costs MUST NOT be counted twice.
A deployment MUST choose and justify its policy for the task and risk.
Every new knowledge or decision artifact MUST record the exact contracts, profiles and rules that materially governed its creation.

A creation-basis record MUST identify the artifact revision, material source revisions, contract and profile definitions, relevant rule-set versions, transformation recipe, responsible actor, creation time or interval, and known gaps.
References MUST resolve to immutable revisions or record the inability to resolve them.
A later adopted rule MUST NOT be inserted into the old basis as though it governed the original work.
The implementation MUST distinguish content change from representation change, assessment change and governance change.
Each proposal MUST identify the previous and proposed rule revisions, motivation, affected scope, expected compatibility, migration implications, evidence, objections and known unresolved questions.
Conflicting adoption decisions MUST block the affected use until a decision maker with authenticated authority resolves the conflict or explicitly adopts a permissible narrower scope.
The decision MUST retain links to the assessed proposal and any restrictions or effective date.
Affected artifacts MUST be classified with the relevant new rule set and use scope.
A compatibility result MUST state the preservation argument or tests.
It MUST preserve negation, conditions, attribution and applicable constraints or declare their loss.
Missing capability or authority MUST remain unknown.
If semantic equivalence has not been established, the migration MUST state that limit even when the new structure is valid.
Publication MUST select a coherent set of artifact revisions, catalogue entries and rendered representations.

A pointer update MUST have an identified adoption decision and the complete atomic [publication guard](../cache-identity-and-invalidation/SPECIFICATION.md#5-guarded-publication-and-serving), including current authority and dependency epochs.
The website, downloadable corpus and API index MUST expose their actual source revisions so a consumer can detect differences.
If a rule was withdrawn because of a known defect or disclosure restriction, a rollback MUST preserve that knowledge and MUST NOT silently reauthorize a previously blocked use.
Each case MUST retain the historical creation basis and the separate current decision.
The document edition, serialized profile, validator implementation, evidence protocol, service build and index snapshot MUST have separately identified versions.

The manifest MUST declare `validation_profile: book-package/2`, and every record MUST use its `KCBookPackageManifest/v2`, `KCBookObject/v2`, `KCBookRelation/v2`, `KCBookEdit/v2` or `KCBookQuality/v2` tag.
A consumer MUST NOT silently reinterpret a version 1 record as version 2.
Its value in producer records MUST remain `not_measured`; the producer cannot grant admission.
The package identifier MUST be a readable lowercase hyphenated slug, 3–96 characters; a single letter followed by digits is forbidden.
Component paths MUST remain relative and inside the package, with no parent traversal or symlinks.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Accepted edits MUST target `readable_md`; `asset_text` has no supported digest-chain semantics and is rejected.
A package without `document_md` and `readable_md` MUST NOT contain accepted edits or a built semantic layer.
Each accepted edit MUST have a nonempty original and replacement, an anchor, basis, reason, actor, input digest and output digest.
At its step, the original MUST occur exactly once, and the replacement MUST occur exactly once in the resulting text.
Applying the accepted edits in ledger order MUST produce `readable.md`; undoing them in reverse order MUST reproduce `document.md` exactly.

JSON readers MUST reject duplicate object member names at every depth, non-finite number tokens and a UTF-8 BOM, so independent readers cannot choose different rights or status values from the same record.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: All comparison and hashing MUST use exact bytes with strict UTF-8 decoding and no newline translation.
A `verified` or `mismatch` integrity declaration MUST include `integrity_check` with `method`, `observer`, `checked_at`, `expected_sha256` and `observed_sha256`.
The observed digest MUST equal the representation digest.
The expected digest MUST NOT be replaced to conceal a mismatch.
A production consumer MUST authenticate the relevant observation at its declared trust boundary before treating it as evidence of source integrity.
`document_md.input_sha256` MUST equal the representation digest and its component record MUST name the converter and version.

Every object MUST retain its text, language, origin, at least one source anchor, status and all eight facet fields: `representation_modes`, `content_kinds`, `discourse_functions`, `aboutness`, `source_position`, `semantic_operators`, `assessment_refs`, and `governance_refs`.
Operators include epistemic and deontic modality, quantifier, negation, condition, exception and order; each operator MUST name its scope.
Each facet MUST be `known` with a value, or `unknown`, `not_applicable` or `withheld` with an explicit reason and no value.
An object named by a package review MUST include that review's identifier in known `assessment_refs`; known-empty cannot deny the very review that cites it.
A `benchmark` claim MUST additionally record corpus, device, tool version, settings, units and mode.
Every relation MUST retain its conditions, origin, evidence, endpoints and status.
A `contradicts` relation MUST include separate `from` and `to` evidence, so one-sided attribution cannot masquerade as a two-sided finding.
A relation touching a stale or rejected endpoint MUST itself be stale or rejected.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Every anchor MUST bind the same representation identifier and source digest as its manifest.
Archives MAY be retained as an unavailable source requiring an adapter, but MUST NOT carry converter output, edits or semantic records under this profile.
A non-author origin MUST have a generation record and `presented_as_author: false`.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: An author statement MUST NOT carry a generation record.
The public Markdown renderer MUST preserve every object and relation field, including qualifiers, operator scopes, source position, conditions, anchors, generation and assessment references.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Payload headings, HTML or apparent origin labels MUST NOT create new rendered record structure.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: A `not_applicable` check MUST state the inapplicability reason in `detail`.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Extraction `pass` MUST contain at least one applicable passing check, no failed or unknown check, and matching seen/expected unit counts when those counts are supplied.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Every semantic review MUST identify `review_id`, `reviewer_id`, `producer_id`, reviewer type, independence basis, time, result, the exact object and relation identifiers examined, and the current object-file, relation-file and readable-file digests.
`sample_size` counts distinct reviewed objects, not relations or checklist items, and MUST equal the object-ID list length.

The `knowledge_ready` profile uses **complete coverage**, not a statistical sample: every object and relation MUST be included, every included record MUST be `reviewed`, the result MUST be `supported`, and the declared reviewer MUST be a human or blind agent distinct from the producer.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: There MUST be at least one object.
The validator MUST compute the first matching row below and require equality with the submitted `package_status`.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: `blocked_integrity`, `bibliography_only` and `adapter_required` MUST omit both document and readable components.
`structure_only`, `partial_pilot` and `knowledge_ready` MUST contain both.
An accepted correction MUST invalidate every object explicitly named in `depends_on_objects` **or** whose source anchor overlaps the edit.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: An affected object MUST be stale or rejected until its `reviewed_edit_ids` explicitly names the accepted corrections and a supported, independent declared review covers that object and the current readable and semantic file digests.
Only `author_open` MAY declare the package publication `license` (`CC-BY-4.0` or `Apache-2.0`) and nonempty `publishable_layers`.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Restricted or unknown works MUST omit that licence field and leave the publication layer list empty.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: The projection function MUST return no rows for such a package.
`candidate_projection(package_directory)` MUST validate a private immutable byte snapshot and compute the rendering from that snapshot itself.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: It MUST return no rows on validation failure or for `blocked_integrity`, `bibliography_only` or `adapter_required`, or without an allowed open publication licence.
The producer MUST NOT widen that scope or treat a candidate row as publication or runtime admission.

The conformance suite MUST retain each regression's expected cause, including negative review, unknown extraction, restricted licence bypass, arbitrary rendering, Markdown structure injection, stale correction, rejected endpoint and obsolete profile.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Existing record tags MUST NOT simply be rewritten: missing observations remain missing, unsupported edits remain unsupported, and review of old bytes does not establish review of migrated bytes.
A migration MUST create a new package release, retain the original revision, identify every mapping or dropped unsupported field, revalidate digests and edits, and obtain any newly required review.
It MUST NOT invent integrity observations, reviewer identities or author attribution.
A chain MUST contain the stages in this order without a gap or a repeat, and MUST start at `intake`; it MAY stop after any stage, and only `classify` and `convert` MAY end `skipped`.

The pipeline key of a document MUST be `d_` followed by the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the original file, as Doclab already writes it, and every receipt of the chain MUST carry that key unchanged.

The `intake` receipt MUST list exactly one input with role `source`, and it MUST be the digest that the key names; a chain whose key is not the digest of its own source is invalid. An `intake` that did not finish and lists no source is not judged.

If a Source Library decision (task E2) chooses a different pipeline key, this section MUST be amended by a pull request that restates the key, the mapping to the names above and the validator rule, and receipts written under this version stay valid under it.
A library-level index of chains MAY exist as a derived view and MUST be rebuildable from them; it never decides a verdict.

An outcome of `done` MUST list at least one input and one output; `skipped` MUST give a reason and list no input and no output; `paused_safe`, `refused` and `failed` MUST give a reason and list no output.
Each receipt after the first MUST carry the SHA-256 of the previous receipt's file bytes, and the first MUST carry null; the order of a chain is the order of its links, never of its file names.

A stage MUST verify the digest of its predecessor's receipt and of each of its own inputs before it writes, and an absent or unverifiable predecessor MUST end the stage as `paused_safe`, not be guessed around.

A stage that finished MUST list among its inputs at least one output of the nearest earlier stage that finished or, for `intake`, `classify`, `convert` and `recognise` only, the original source; no later stage MAY list the original source as an input.
No receipt MAY follow a receipt whose outcome is `paused_safe`, `refused` or `failed`.
A stage MUST NOT finish before it started or start before its predecessor finished.

The `recognise` stage MAY be performed by an import adapter that verifies existing recognition outputs against the source bytes now, instead of running recognition. The receipt of such an adapter MUST name the import in `tool.name` (a name ending in `-import`), MUST give the actual start and finish of the verification as `started_at` and `finished_at`, MUST list as `outputs` the existing recognition outputs that were verified, each by the SHA-256 of its exact bytes, and MUST list as `inputs` what PIP-R009 allows (the source when `classify` and `convert` were skipped, otherwise an output of the nearest earlier stage that finished) and MAY list the earlier evidence files by digest.

An import receipt that finished MUST carry the measurement `recognition_executed` as measured with the value `false`, and the measurements `original_run_id` and `original_finished_at`, each either measured (read from the earlier evidence) or `not_measured` with a reason. A quality or damage figure taken from the earlier evidence MUST be named `recorded_` followed by its name and is a figure as recorded, never one measured again by the import.

A receipt whose tool does not name an import MUST NOT claim `recognition_executed` as `false`; a receipt whose tool names an import, whatever its outcome, MUST NOT claim `recognition_executed` as anything but measured `false`; a receipt MUST NOT carry the measurements `recognition_executed`, `original_run_id` or `original_finished_at` twice; and an import adapter exists for the `recognise` stage only.

A chain with an imported `recognise` is a new chain for the same document key: it starts at `intake` with the source hashed at the time of the import, `classify` and `convert` MAY end `skipped` (PIP-R001), the earlier recognition outputs and evidence are kept unchanged and referenced by digest only, and the rights rules of PIP-R012 and PIP-R027 apply to it as to any chain (the receipts carry the rights state known at each stage, which for an imported book is `unknown`, or `third_party_restricted` when that is known; the determination of the work's rights is in the package's rights record). A receipt never claims work that was not done: a stage that did not run is recorded `skipped` with its reason where PIP-R001 allows it (`classify` and `convert`), and otherwise the chain stops; the imported `recognise` (and, under PIP-R028, a verify-only `bundle`) records work that was verified rather than performed, and says so by its measurements. This is a rule of the producer; the checker reads the measurements only. A consumer that needs recognition to have been executed MUST read `recognition_executed`; a checker that accepts the chain does not say that it was. The absence of the measurement means that it is not established, never that recognition ran, and a `true` is the producer's statement; an import presented under the name of an ordinary recognition tool and without the measurement cannot be told from a run by its receipt. The checker reads receipts only: that the verified outputs match the source bytes is established by the importer at the time of the import and by nothing in the chain. The recorded-figure naming, the choice of the rights class and a non-empty `original_run_id` are rules of the producer that the checker does not enforce, and the match of `-import` is exact and case-sensitive.

In a chain whose `recognise` is an import, the `bundle` stage MAY verify an existing bundle instead of assembling it, and when it does it MUST record that with the measurements `bundle_assembled` measured `false` and `bundle_verified` measured `true`, and lists the verified bundle manifest by the SHA-256 of its exact bytes as its output; its tool does not name an import (PIP-R025 allows that name on `recognise` only). The two measurements are carried together on the `bundle` stage and nowhere else, each measured `true` or `false`, and `bundle_assembled` `false` is valid only after an imported `recognise`; an ordinary bundle stage needs neither. The checker reads the two measurements, that they are booleans, that they are carried on the `bundle` stage and that `bundle_assembled` `false` follows an imported `recognise`; it does not check that the output is the hash of the verified manifest (only that the next stage consumes it) and it does not look at the outcome of the bundle receipt, so that the verification really took place is the producer's statement; a bundle that was verified and carries neither measurement reads as an ordinary assembly.

A stage MAY keep the rights class of its predecessor or narrow it, and MUST NOT widen it; from least to most permissive the classes are `third_party_restricted`, `unknown`, and then `public_domain` and `author_open`, which are equally open.

The rights class a receipt carries MUST be the rights state known at that stage, and a determination of the rights of a work (for example `public_domain` with its evidence) MUST be made only in the package's rights record, never in a receipt; a chain that starts at `unknown` does not end at `public_domain`, and the receipt classes and the package's rights record are read separately. The checker refuses only a widening of the class along a chain (PIP-R012); that a receipt carries the state known at its stage, and that a determination is made in the package's rights record and not in a receipt, are rules of the producer that it does not check: a chain whose receipts all carry `public_domain` is not refused by it, and a reader MUST take the rights of a work from the package's rights record.

requirements.section: 9. Public-domain works and declared damage in `book-package/2`
requirements.text: The damage list travels with the package and is shown wherever the package is shown; a library that publishes a package with declared damage MUST publish the list with it and MUST NOT present the package as clean.

A classification result MUST name the taxonomy `kc-doc-class/1` and the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the canon file, and a result that names another taxonomy identifier or another digest MUST be refused and MUST NOT be read against the latest canon.

A `classified` result MUST carry exactly one class and exactly that class as its only candidate, an `ambiguous` result MUST carry no class, at least two distinct candidates and a reason, and an `unknown` result MUST carry no class, no candidate and a reason.

(A rule of the classifier's behaviour, not one the schema or the checker can verify.) A classifier MUST NOT use the class `other` for a source whose class is uncertain, and MUST NOT choose between candidates by an arbitrary priority; it MUST record the alternatives it found.

A result MUST NOT carry an invented number as confidence: when no calibrated assessment exists it MUST say `not_measured` with a reason, and a measured score MUST name its method, its version and its interpretation.

A result MUST identify, by SHA-256 and by a selector, a rule or a feature, the representation that was actually inspected, and MUST state whether the coverage of the unit is complete, partial or not measured.

The classify receipt of a finished stage MUST list the exact bytes of the result as one output with the role `classification` and their `sha256`, and the receipt schema MUST NOT gain a field for a class or a taxonomy.
A stage that needs a particular content class MUST NOT proceed on an `ambiguous` or an `unknown` result by choosing a class itself.

A classification MUST NOT change the rights class, the declared damage, the `knowledge_ready` status, publication, indexing or `kc2_admission` of the document; it is provenance for later stages and never an admission.

A classification under a later taxonomy MUST be a new result for the same document key with its own receipt chain, the earlier results MUST be kept, and a change of storage location MUST change neither the key nor the class.
Conformance MUST name the implemented profile, exact implementation revision and assessed requirements; publication of these requirements does not establish that conformance.

**Request binding.** A service offering a ready Knowledge Contract MUST bind the request to the task and requirements revision, intended recipient and use, applicable constraints, required profiles, temporal mode, and resource limits.
Where any required value is unknown, it MUST report the gap or obtain the missing information before asserting admission for that use.

**Response and outcome.** The response MUST identify the exact contract and representation versions, selected knowledge revisions, sources and grounds, mandatory dependency closure, coverage, omitted or unresolved obligations, applicable constraints, assessments and the decision's trust boundary.

Its operation outcome MUST be one of **`success`, `partial`, `refused`, `failed`, `unresolved`**, with the [status model's meanings](../../engineering/specifications/status-model/SPECIFICATION.md#3-canonical-dimension-vocabularies).
`ready` is an availability or lifecycle state; it MUST NOT replace an outcome token.
**Admission scope.** A ready-for-use assertion MUST be backed by the mandatory checks for the declared use.

The **Knowledge Contract admission runtime** is the service boundary responsible for such a decision; its actual implementation and profile versions MUST be identified rather than inferred from the publication edition or the legacy field `kc2_admission`.
**Execution binding.** If the contract is issued for execution, the system MUST subsequently bind the actual attempt, actor, environment, contract revision, outputs, effects and acceptance evidence.
A deployment MUST build those pages from the declared commit and reject an uncommitted or mismatched source tree.
A client MUST establish repository identity before comparing a result's source revision with the reader's publication commit.
It MUST NOT be applied to an unrelated source.
Unknown and different revisions MUST be distinguished from a match.
A client MUST NOT substitute an untrusted title, branch label or bare hash for that identity.
If URL revision and `source_revision` conflict, it MUST report a mismatch.

Refreshing or promoting the backend index is a separate operation. **Admission governance.** An indexing operation MUST use the repository's existing publication-decision and allowlist process; a catalogue entry is not a substitute for that approval.
**Release gate.** Before a release is described as consistently indexed, the operator MUST record all six checks below against the exact source revision.
**Receipt.** A gate record conforming to **`KCIndexReleaseReceipt/v1`** MUST satisfy the [receipt JSON Schema](index-release-receipt.schema.json) and the semantic checks here.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: Query IDs, admitted paths, and record IDs within each results or fetch list MUST be unique.
The same record MAY be found by several different queries.
Each query's expected paths MUST be drawn from `admitted_paths`; every expected path MUST have a matching result before `query_coverage` can pass.
Each retained result MUST identify the declared repository and `source_revision`, and its source path and `source_sha256` MUST match the admitted snapshot.
A service returning passages MUST provide both bindings or leave the relevant check unknown.
Every result MUST have a matching fetch identity and representation hash before `fetch_identity` can pass.
Every superseded record's observed status MUST equal its required status before `supersession` can pass.
**Presentation.** The default result view SHOULD show the passage, human title, source link and indexed revision.
Technical evidence about admission, uncertainty and score semantics MAY be placed in an accessible details section.
Material limits MUST remain visible where they change a user's decision.
A retrieval score MUST NOT be presented as a probability that a claim is true without an independently established calibration and its scope.
Scientific reading SHOULD remain possible without making API calls: full pages, equations, references and evidence links are served as the static selected edition.
**Acceptance cases.** The integration MUST reject a site build from the wrong source commit, a dirty publication tree, a missing referenced document and a local link escaping the publication.
Search presentation MUST distinguish a matching Knowledge Contract revision, an older revision, an unknown revision and a record from another repository.
Rendering MUST preserve equations, tables, footnotes and document anchors.

Receipt validation MUST reject omitted checks, a passing decision with a nonpassing check, an ambiguous repository/revision identity, duplicate identities, missing expected paths, and a mismatched fetch readback.
requirements.verification_scope: finite regression examples; not a conformance certificate

requirements.text: A contract-delivery acceptance suite MUST additionally exercise missing constraints, a mandatory unknown profile, incomplete closure, insufficient budget, revoked disclosure authority, stale source evidence, and a correct informational response that does not authorize execution.
